correctness.rationale: PASS: For n>=3, graph M_{2n}=C_{2n} with antipodal chords; square joins vertices at distance at most two. Any four-color square coloring makes each closed neighborhood (size four) rainbow, so each color class is a radius-one efficient dominating set. The direct x_{i-1}+x_i+x_{i+1}+x_{i+n}=1 equations force n=2 mod 4, and i mod 4 colors validly for every such n>=6. For n=8 no independent four-set exists in the square (otherwise a perfect code), so with 16 vertices alpha<=3 implies chi>=6. At n=3,4 the squared graphs are K6,K8. The explicit two-row words for n=5,7,8,9,12 are valid, and replicating the first four columns of the 7,9,12 words repeats only already validated local three-column patterns; the crossed seam stays unchanged. This covers all remaining odd n>=5 and multiples of four n>=12, hence the whole classification. Independent direct circular graph construction checked all five base words, extensions through n=50, every four-residue case in that range, and 0 independent four-sets for n=8.

originality.rationale: PASS, best of knowledge: Knor et al. Lemma 2.2 already proves exactly which Möbius ladders admit efficient domination; this yields the four-color necessary condition but not full five-color upper bounds or the exceptional n=8 six-color classification. Other inspected papers study interval edge coloring, strong edge coloring, locating coloring or untwisted toroidal grid squares and do not dominate the present square vertex chromatic formula. A differently indexed circulant-square coloring classification remains a real originality risk.
residual_risks: A general square-chromatic theorem for the circulant Ci_{2n}(1,2,n-1,n), perhaps under L(1,1) coloring terminology, could reproduce the formula.
Previously published efficient-domination lemma is explicitly credited and cannot be claimed new.
